- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in the following 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., 3–5% gap over 5+ days), consider “mean reversion bias” — increase forecast by 1–3% in next period if sentiment remains neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price movements (especially after sentiment turns positive); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment >0.4.
- If sentiment history shows rapid reversal (e.g., from negative to positive in 3–5 days), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match sentiment shift within 1–2 periods.
